en.headline: Abby Choi trial hears Kwong Kau claim he transferred HK$30 million for flat purchase
en.dek: The former father-in-law told the High Court on Tuesday that the money went towards a Kadooria flat registered in his name, and that a large soup pot was intended as a planter.
body: Kwong Kau, the former father-in-law of slain socialite Abby Choi, told the High Court on Tuesday that he had transferred about HK$30 million to Choi to help buy a flat at the Kadooria development in Ho Man Tin.

Taking the witness stand in the murder and dismemberment trial, Kwong said the flat was registered in his name because he did not own another property in Hong Kong at the time. He claimed the large soup pot later found at a village flat was purchased to hold plants, and that knives were bought so he could slice meat himself to avoid bacteria on market chopping boards.

Kwong remains on trial for murder alongside his sons Anthony Kwong and Alex Kwong, Choi’s former husband. Both sons have previously pleaded guilty to preventing the lawful burial of Choi’s body. Kwong has pleaded guilty to illegally disposing of the body.
The trial continues. All three men deny the murder charge.

zh.headline: 蔡天鳳案鄧球作供稱曾轉賬三千萬助購嘉道理山單位
zh.dek: 前家翁周二在高等法院稱款項用於購買以他名義登記的單位，並指大湯煲是用來種植植物。
body: 蔡天鳳前家翁鄧球周二在高等法院作供時表示，他曾向蔡天鳳轉賬約三千萬元，協助購買何文田嘉道理山的單位。
鄧球在謀殺案審訊中說，因為當時他在香港沒有其他物業，所以單位以他的名義登記。他聲稱現場發現的大湯煲是用來種植植物，而刀具則是為了自己切肉，以免市場砧板細菌多。
鄧球與其兩名兒子鄧港傑及鄧港杰（蔡天鳳前夫）一同被控謀殺。兩名兒子較早前已承認阻止合法埋葬屍體，鄧球亦已承認非法處理屍體。
審訊繼續。三人均否認謀殺控罪。
